t: Principal & Prop. of the Kokumin Ei-Gakukai (National English Language Association) in Tokyo; b. 1861 in Oita-ken; studied English at Keio Gijuku for several years; organized the above English School in conjunction with a certain foreigner in '88. Add. Koj. Sambancho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. & Prof. of Hiroshima Higher Technical School; b. 1871 in Fukuoka-ken; grad. in Civil Eng., Tokyo Imp. Univ., '95; sent to U.S.A. and France for study; civil engineer of Kumamoto-ken, '96; Prof. of the 5th High School, '00; next Dir. of Kumamoto Higher Tech. School. Add. Hiroshima.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: ex-Dir. of Tokyo Deaf and Dumb Sch.; b. 1854 in Niigata-ken; grad. from the Tokyo Higher Normal Sch., '79; instructor at Chiba Mid. Sch., and then Tokyo Women's Higher Normal Sch.; Dir. of Tokyo Deaf & Dumb School, '93-29. Add. Koishikawa Sasugaya-cho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: B.A., lady Director of Doshisha University (Kyoto) since '19; b. 1868 in Tango; studied at the Kyoto Prefectural Girls' High School and then at the Doshisha Girls' College; taught English at a certain mission school in Yokohama; further studied at the Bryn Mawr Coll., Penn.; teacher at Kobe Jogakuin, '99; Head of English Literature Dept., Doshisha Girls' College, and then the present post. Add. Doshisha, Kyoto.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Pres. of Seoul Imperial Univ.; b. 1872 at Uwajima; grad. in Law, Tokyo Imp. Univ., '98; Secretary at Tokyo Prefectural Office and at the Department of Education, '98-11; sent to Germany, '07 to inquire into education matters; Dir. of Special Edu. Bureau, '12-24; Vice-Min. of Education, '24-27. Add. Seoul, Chosen.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: adopted son of late Miwata Masako (lady educationalist) and Principal of Miwata Girls' High School; b. 1872 in Kagawa-ken; grad. from Philosophy and Sociology, Tokyo Imp. Univ., class '01. Add. Kojimachi Sanbancho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. of 3rd High School; b. 1866 in Ishikawa-ken; grad. from the Coll. of Science (mathematics), Tokyo Imp. Univ., '11; Lecturer of Tokyo Higher Commercial School; taught at Miye Middle School, '83; Prof. at Third High School, '95; Prof. at Peers' School, '09; studied in Germany, England and America, '09-11; Principal of Kyoto 1st Middle School, '11; the present post since '22. Add. Yoshida Hommachi, Kyoto.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Litt., Dir. of Tokyo Academy of Music; b. 186[illegible] in Oita-ken; edu. in history, Tokyo Imp. Univ., '95; Prof. of Spanish in Tokyo School for Foreign Languages, '00; Dir. of the same School, '08. Add. Nagasaki-machi, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. of Tokyo School of Foreign Languages; b. 1876 in Gifu-ken; grad. from Lit. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., '97; was Prof. of 4th School and Hiroshima Higher Normal School; then School Inspector; sent abroad for observation of educational affairs, '27. Add. Nakano, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. Osaka Foreign Lang. School; b. 1874 in Miyagi-ken; grad. from Tokyo Imp. Univ. (German Literature), '03; studied in Europe; Prof. at 4th High Sch., Hiroshima Higher Normal Sch., Dir. of Matsuyama High Sch. and then present post (since '21); toured abroad on official mission, '27. Add. Osaka,

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. of Matsuye Higher School; b. in Toyama-ken; grad. from Lit. Tokyo Imp. Univ., '04; School-Inspector and then Secretary of the Education Dept.; the present post in '24. Add. Matsuye, Shimane-ken.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. of the Imperial Museum; b. 1871 in Tokyo; grad. in Philosophy, Tokyo Imp. Univ., '94; successively filled the posts of Educational Inspector, Dir. of the Tokyo Music Academy, Dir. of the 8th High School, etc., Dir. of Peeress' School, '20-24; present post in '24. Add. Azabu Hiro-o, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: educationist and English scholar, Pres. of Seisoku English Language School; b. 1866 in Miyagi-ken; edu. first at the Kobu Daigaku about five years, but left it unfinished; instructor at the 1st Higher Sch., '88 and the Kokumin Eigakkai; founded the present school in '96. Works: a number of text books on English grammar, an English-Japanese dictionary and other works. Add. Kojimachi Gobancho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Agr., Ph. D. (Johns Hopkins'), Pres. of Hokkaido Univ. (Sapporo) since its creation; b. 1855 in Iwate-ken; grad. from the then existing Foreign Language School, '76, and the Sapporo Agr. Coll., '80; further studied agri. economy at Johns Hopkins' and in Germany '82-87; Professor in the Sapporo Coll. on returning home; became its President, '94; American exchange prof., '14. Add. Sapporo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Madam. Dir. Jissen Girls' School and Pres. of Women's Patriotic Association since '20; a Court maid of honour when about 16 years old, and again after the death of her husband. An instructor of the Peeress' School; resigned in Nov. '07; and has since devoted herself chiefly to a private female school she founded about '99; visited Europe, '93-95. Add. Aoyama Kitamachi, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D.C.L., Crown Mem. House of Peers (nom. '15). President of Waseda Univ.; b. 1860 at Tokyo; grad. at Law, Tokyo Imp. Univ., '82; has since been connected with Waseda Univ., which was started the same year by Marquis Okuma; was once one of the leading members of the Progressionists, but for years past kept aloof from active politics, devoting himself to affairs of the Univ.; was Director of the Commercial Bureau, For. Office, '96-97 and Senior Counsellor of Education, '98; was repeatedly returned to the House from Saitama-ken; toured in Europe and America, '14; Minister of Education in the Okuma Cabinet, '15-16. Add. Komagome, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D.C.L., M.A. (Columbia), Chairman, Board of Dir. Waseda Univ.; b. 1875 in Nagano-ken; grad. from Waseda, '96 and further studied in America, England and Germany, '01-03; once connected with the Yomiuri and was also the editor-in-chief of the Nichi Nichi; toured abroad, '21-22. Add. Ushigome Benten-cho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. of Kobe University of Commerce; b. in Nagasaki-ken; grad. Tokyo Higher Com. School, class '01; Lecturer at the alma mater for about a year; sent to England for study, '02-06; Prof. at Nagasaki Higher Com. School, '06; at Kobe Higher Com. School, '08; visited Europe in '14 and England in '23; Dir. of Kobe High. Com. Sch., '25; present post, in Apr. '29. Add. Kobe Univ. of Commerce.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Pres. of Family School, Dir. of Central Association of Social Works; b. 1868 in Tokyo; grad. at Doshisha Theological School in '88, christian preacher for years; stud. in America, '95-99; visited Europe to study social works in '03; created Family School to reform fallen women. Add. Nishi-Sugamo, near Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: lady educationist and founder of the Joshi Eigaku-juku (Girls' English School) in Tokyo; b. 1865 in Tokyo, daughter of the late Tsuda Sen, an agriculturist; was among the first batch of girls sent to U.S.A. for study by Government, '71-82; teacher in the Peers' School and lecturer in the Women's Higher Normal School on returning home; has frequently visited America. Add. Kojimachi Goban-cho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. Nagoya Higher Com. Sch.; b. 1866 in Niigata-ken; grad. from Tokyo Semmon Gakko (now Waseda Univ.), '87; studied Ethics in U.S.A. and Germany; was Prof. of Tokyo Academy of Music, Tokyo Higher Normal School, and Dir. of the former school, successively; was despatched to China in '13, and to Europe and America, '20. Add. Nagoya.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Pres. of Tokyo Women's College; b. 1870 in Tokyo; grad. from the Tokyo Female Higher Normal School, '90; studied in England, '96; was Prof. of Tokyo Female Higher Normal School for many years. Add. Uyenohara, Nakano-machi, near Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. Tokyo High Sch.; b. 1863 in Saga; first studied Medicine at Tokyo Imp. Univ., but left it without finishing in '84; held post of prof. at various Gov. Schools or Dir. of Middle Schools; Dir. Imperial Academy of Music, '08-17; Dir. Tokyo Higher Girls' Normal Sch., '17-21; present post since '22. Add. Yoyogi Tomigaya, near Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. of the Teikoku Electric Light Co., Mng. of Tokyo Branch of L. J. Healing & Co., Ltd. (London); b. 1875 in Mie-ken; grad. from the now defunct Post & Telegraph School, '02 and entered Govt. service; then resigning the post entered Messrs. Healing as Mng. Add. Shiba Takanawa, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. of Tokyo Electric Light Co., ex-Dir. of Tokyo Municipal Electric Office; b. 1879 in Shiga-ken; grad. in Law, Kyoto Imp. Univ. in '03; Private Secretary to Home Minister, '04; Councillor and then Secretary of the Dept. of Communications; Chief of the General Affairs Section of the Kobe Railway Control Bureau; Councillor and then Director of the Imp. Railway Board, '15-16; present post in '26. Add. Ushigome Haramachi, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dr. Eng. (Japan), Pres. Iwakuni Elec. Tram. and Tokyo Elec. Cos.; b. in 1856; grad. from Tokyo Engineering College in '81; appointed its Professor, '84; retired '86 to start electric business; chief electrician to the Tokyo Electric Light Co. in '92 and founder of the Tokyo Street Railway Co.; has been to Europe and America several times for study, on business, etc. and was under Edison for some while. Add. Azabu Higashicho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: ex-M.P., Pres. of Daido Elec. Power Co., etc., brother-in-law of the Fukuzawa brothers, being husband of their sister; b. 1864 at Kawagoye; studied at Keio; and further at a Commercial Coll. in U.S.A.; returning home in '89, he first entered Tokyo Ice Works, then Oji Paper Mill, and finally Hokkaido Colliery & Steamship Co., of which he was agent for Tokyo. Add. Shibuya-machi, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: 2nd Baron, Mem. House of Peers, Pres. of Tokyo Electric Light Co., and Oriental Steel Foundry, dir. of various Cos.; b. 1863 in Tokyo, son of late Junzo Go; studied in Europe; after several years in Govt. service he entered business circles; was chairman of Tokyo Stock Ex. till '24. Add. Koj. Kaminibancho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: B.A. (Cambridge), founder of Inawashiro Hydro-Elec. Power Co.; b. 1872 in Wakayama-ken; grad. Keio Univ., '91 and Waseda, '94; further studied at Cambridge; M.P. in '04 from Wakayama-ken. Add. Koj. Shimo-rokubancho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. Daido Electric Power Co., Mem. Kobe Chamber of Commerce; b. 1863 in Tokyo, younger brother to the late Baron Haruo Itami; early entered the N.Y.K. being later promoted to be Mng. of its Kobe Branch. Add. Shimo-Yamate-dori, Kobe.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: electrician and Mng.-Dir. of the Nippon Electric Co., (joint undertaking between Japanese and foreign capitalists in which the Western-Electric Co., U.S.A., are prominent); b. 1854 in Fukuoka; grad. from the former Govt. Engineering Coll., '82, and entered the present Co. on its formation about '93. Add. Azabu Fujimicho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. of Keio Electric R'ly Co., &c.; b. 1870, eldest son of Takeshi Kawada (learned scholar of Chinese classics); studied at Michigan in '96. Add. Ushigome Wakamiya-cho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Pres. of Osaka Elec. Power Co., Vice-Pres. of Daido Elec. Power Co.; b. 1868 in Shizuoka-ken; engaged in printing business in his early years, besides shared in Daido Fertilizer Co., Tateyama Hydro-Elec. Co., etc. Shibuya-machi, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Vice-Pres. of Toho Electric Power Co., Dir. of Toho Gas Co., etc.; b. 1875 in Iki; grad. from Keio Univ. in '00; entered the Bank of Japan., '00; afterwards established a firm and carried on coal business in Kobe and Osaka over ten years; founded an electric railway concern in Fukuoka, Kyushu in '90. Add. Shimoochiai, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. Furukawa Elec. Industry Co.; b. 1874 in Okayama-ken and was adopted into the family; studied at Waseda and entered Furukawa Firm; branch manager at Osaka and Shanghai, and then Dir. of Business Section of the Head Office, etc.; stayed in England. Add. Koj. Ichi-Bancho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Mem. House of Peers, Chairman Kokkatsu (International Film) Co.; b. 1874 in Yamagata-ken; grad. in Law, Tokyo Imp. Univ., '08 and passed civil service exam. same year; was in service of provincial govts. before his app. to Governor of Tochigi-ken; then Governor of Karafuto, '14; Sup't. of Metropolitan Police, '16-18. Add. Aoyama Takagi-cho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Pres. of Miye Electric Co., and of Kei-Han Electric R'ly. Co., Dir. of Daido Electric Power Co., Shin Kei-Han R'ly. Co.; b. 1874 in Yamaguchi; adopted son of Kosaburo Ota; grad. in Law, Tokyo Imp. Univ., '98; Secy. of Imp. Railway Board and later entered the Kei-Han Electric Co., Ltd., as its Mng. Dir. in '06. Add. Kei-Han Office, Osaka.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Pres. of Kinugawa Hydro-Elec. Co., Dir. of Tokyo Gas Co., etc.; b. 1863 in Oita-ken; edu. at Meiji Univ.; became lawyer and struggled his way up to success; once M.P., but soon resigned to enter business; Dir. of the then Tokyo Railway Co.; is also Pres. of Odawara Express Elec. Railway Co. started '27. Add. Kami Osaki, near Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. Keisei Electric R'ly. Co., Borneo Rubber Co., Japan Electro-Industrial Co., etc.; b. 1860 in Oita-ken; grad. from the Oita Normal School and Tokyo Semmon Gakko (forerunner of Waseda Univ.); passed the Exam. for Bar and began practice in Tokyo; once returned M.P. Add. Koishikawa Shin-Suwacho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Crown Mem. House of Peers (since '27), Pres. of Tokyo Electric Light Co., Dir. of Naigai Kogyo, Tokyo Taxi-Cab, Nippon Seima, and other concerns; b. in 1873 and adopted into the family '96 by marriage; studied at the Chuo Daigaku. Add. Mita, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Pres. of Osaka Elec. Lamp Bulb Co., and Uwa Hydro-Elec. Co.; b. 1859 in Ehime-ken; grad. from Keiogijuku in 1881; Vice-Consul at Wonsan (Korea), '82; Comptroller of the Patent Bureau of the Agr. & Com. Dept., '89; Dir. of the Nagasaki Post and Telegraph Office, '91; returned to the Lower House seven times; Mayor of Sasebo City, '02-06; afterwards entered business. Add. Kojimachi-ku Hirakawa-cho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dr. Eng., M.A. (Cornell), Prof. at Engineering Dept., Kyushu Imp. Univ.; b. 1878 in Yokohama; grad. from the Eng. Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ., '00; lecturer at his alma mater the same year; sent to Germany, England and U.S.A. for study, '08-10; present post since '11. Works: Science of Electrical Engineering. Add. Jigyo-nishi-machi, Fukuoka city.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Eng., Director of Naval Arsenal, Prof. at Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. 1867 in Tokyo; edu. at the University, class '90; sent by the Navy to France where he studied at Hotchkiss; devised a new plug for quickfires; sent twice to England on official business. Add. Tamagawa, Ebara-gun, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dr. Eng., Emeritus Prof. of Waseda; b. 1859 at Okayama; edu. in electricity at the Govt. Eng. College, class '81; electrician to Department of Communications till '16; was despatched to Europe and America two or three times. Add. Azabu Kogai-cho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Architect, Hon. Mem. of Society of Architects (London), and of Royal Society of Arts (London); b. 1868 at Yonezawa; grad. at Eng. Coll. (Architecture), Tokyo Imp. Univ.; further studied at Cambridge (Eng.); on returning home entered Edu. Dept.; again studied in England, '03-07 opened Sone-Chujo Office, '08, besides his own. Add. Komagome Hayashi-cho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Baron (cr. 1919), Dr. Eng., Mem. Imperial Academy, Privy Councillor since '24; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. 1854 at Himeji; studied engineering in France, '75-80; was successively Director of the Public Works Bureau (Home Office); Vice-Minister of Communications, Director-General of the Government Railways and Director of Seoul-Fusan R'ly., '03-07; Pres. of Tokyo Subway Co. till '25. He is one of the best amateur “no” singers and actors. Add. Hongo Yumi-cho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Eng., Architect, Emeritus Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ. b. 1864 in Yamagata-ken; grad. from Architecture at the University, '92; despatched to China, India and Turkey in '02-05 to study his special subject. Add. Hongo Nishikatamachi, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dr. Eng., Prof. at Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. 1870 in Ehime; grad. in Mechanical Eng., Tokyo Imp. Univ., class '94; further studied his speciality in England and France; Prof. at 3rd High School, etc. Add. Kyoto Imp. Univ.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Eng., Prof. at Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. 1884 in Saitama-ken; grad. from Electrical Engineering Course of Tokyo Imp. Univ., '07; first a technical expert of communications; then Assist.-Prof. of Tokyo Imp. Univ.; stayed in Germany, England and America for study. Add. Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Eng., ex-Chairman of Board of the South Manchuria R'ly. Co., '13-19; b. 1864 in Kochi-ken; grad. in '89 from Eng. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; engineer of the nationalized Kyushu R'ly. Co., '89; Eng. to the Railway Department, '92-05; Vice-Pres. of the South M. R'ly., '06-18; Pres. of same, '18-22. Add. Okubo, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dr. Eng., Mng.-Dir. of Mitsui Mining Co., Electro-Chemical Industry Co., Hokkaido Iron Works, etc.; b. 1871 in Osaka; grad. in Mining, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; entered Mitsui firm as expert, gradually rising to the present eminence. Add. Azabu Kita-Higakubo, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Eng., Prof. at Eng. Coll. of the Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. 1871 in Hokkaido; grad. from the Eng. Coll. of the Tokyo Imp. Univ., '93; appointed Prof. at 3rd High School, '96; Assist.-Prof. at Kyoto Imp. Univ., '97; sent to Germany for study, '99; Prof. at Science and Eng. Coll. of the Kyoto Imp. Univ., '01; Prof. at Eng. Coll. of the same Univ. since '14. Add. Kyoto.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Eng., Prof. at Waseda Univ. since '10, Mem. of Govt. Earthquake Committee; b. 1886 in Yamanashi-ken; edu. in Architecture, Tokyo Imp. Univ., class '10; further studied Ferro-concrete and allied construction at the Institute of Technology, Boston, '16-18. Works: Earthquake-proof Construction of Skeleton Structure, Aug. '24; The Theory of Structure and of Building Construction, 9th June, '25 (both in Japanese). Add. Waseda Univ.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Eng., Emeritus Prof. at Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. 1860 in Tokyo; edu. at now defunct Eng. College in '82; assist. architect in building the Imperial Palace, '83-86; Professor of the University combining a post in the Home Office; studied in Europe, '92-98; sent in '97 to Assam, India, to study architecture as affected by earthquake, and also to Naples in '09 on a similar mission. Add. Koishikawa Haramachi, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Eng., (Civil Eng.), Emeritus Prof. at the Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. 1867 in Aichi-ken; grad. from the University with honours in '88; engineer to the Kwansai R'ly Co. for some years; studied further his speciality in Germany and other countries, '96-98. Add. Hongo Nishikata-machi, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Eng.; b. 1876 in Kobe; grad. from Civil Eng., Tokyo Imp. Univ., class '09; Engineer to the Tokyo City Office the same year; despatched abroad in '02 to inspect harbor construction work in Europe and America, returning home, '03; Chief of Public Work Section of the Tokyo City Office; then Eng. of the Finance Dept.; attached to the Construction Bureau, '06; in charge of the Yokohama harbor work, '08; Eng. to the Tokyo City Office, '11; Chief of the Osaka Harbor Work Office and also of the City Planning Office, till '24; Dir. of the Reconstruction Bureau, '24-25; adviser to the same, '25-26. Add. Reconstruction Bureau.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Eng., Dir. and Prof. of the Kiryu Higher Tech. School, Prop. of the Nishida Laboratory; b. 1877 in Tokyo; grad. in applied chemistry, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; further studied at the School of Technology in Manchester, and Ecole de Chimie, Mulhouse, Alsace; was Prof. of the Nagoya High. Technical Coll.; Mng.-Dir. of the Nippon Celluloid Co. Add. Kojimachi Junichome, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: 2nd Visc. (suc. '07), D. Eng., Prof. at Eng. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., '04-25; Mem. of House of Peers; b. 1878 at Toyohashi; grad. from the said college, '03; further studied in Germany and France, '08-11; sent to Tsingtao to prosecute scientific investigation there during the 1914 War; Senior Secretary of Navy, '20 and Head of Scientific Investigation Office since '21. Add. Uyeno Yanaka Shimizucho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Eng. (Architecture), Consulting Architect to the Mitsubishi Firm for whom he has designed a large number of buildings; b. 1870 in Tokyo; edu. at Tokyo Imp. Univ., in Architecture, class '95. Add. Ichigaya Nakano-cho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Eng. (Architecture), Prof. at Waseda Univ. since '10; b. 1878 in Tochigi-ken; edu. at Tokyo Imp. Univ. in Architecture, class '10; travelled in Europe and America, '10-11; 1st prize designs of the Tokyo City Hall, etc. Add. Koishikawa Sasugaya-cho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Baron, D. Eng., Prof. of Shipbuilding at Tokyo Imp. Univ., and consulting engineer to the Kawasaki Dockyard; b. 1872 in Kaga; grad. from the Tokyo Imp. Univ., '95, and afterward studied at the Central Technical College, London, and also at Humphrey, and Tennant's Works and finally at Berlin; undertook the designing of the Toyo Kisen Kaisha's sister steamers, Tenyo and Chiyo. Add. Hongo Akebono-cho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Eng., Emeritus Prof. at Tokyo Imp. Univ., ex-Dir. of State Industrial Laboratory, etc.; b. 1855 in Tokyo; grad. at Chemistry, Tokyo Imp. Univ., '78; further studied at Owens Coll., Manchester, and at Berlin Univ., returning home in '82; Prof. at his alma mater and other institutions; retired in '05; the Pres. of Tokyo Gas Co., '05-15. Add. Hongo Higashikatamachi, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Eng. (Metallurgy), Mem. of Imperial Academy, Emeritus Prof. of Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. 1872 in Shimane-ken; grad. from above institution, class '97, and after some years' further studies in Germany, was appointed Prof. at his alma mater. Add. Tokyo Imp. Univ.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Eng., ex-Dean of the Eng. Coll. and Prof. of Architecture, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. 1869 in Kyoto; grad. from Tokyo Imp. Univ., '93; further studied in England, Germany and France, '99-02; Prof. at the alma mater on his return. Add. Koishikawa Hisakatacho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Eng., C.E., B.S., Pres. Ishikawajima Dockyard Co., Dir. Keihan Elec. Rly.; b. 1853 in Nagano-ken; grad. in '83; Govt. Eng. College; conferred C.E. and B.S. by Glasgow Univ., class '89; studied practical side under Sir John Fowler and other noted British engineers; elected member of Civil Engineering Society, London. Add. Akasaka Omote-cho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Eng., Prof. Tohoku Imp. Univ.; b. in Kyoto; grad. in Elec. Eng., Tokyo Imp. Univ., class '09; was Prof. of the Sendai Higher Technical School; then studied in England. Add. Ryokakuin-cho, Sendai City.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Aud. of Russo-Japanese Fishery Co., Ex-Sec. of the Bank of Chosen; b. 1878 in Ehime-ken; grad. from the Law Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ., and on graduation entered the service of the Chosen Bank, in which he had charge of a Branch at Fusan and other places; later Sectional Chief of the head office; removed to the present post. Add. Hisakata-machi, Koishikawa, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Pres. of Japan Chemical Industry Co., Ltd.; b. 1870 in Tottori-ken; grad. from Keio Univ., '92; entered the Jiji Shimpo with which he was connected for about nineteen years; then became a Dir. of the Japan Conscription Ins. Co., Ltd. Add. Shirokane Sanko-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. S.M.R. since '22; b. 1869; grad. from Tokyo Higher Commercial School, '04 and took to business; Dept. Chief of the Mitsui Bussan till '21. Add. Dairen.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Prop. of Amano Railway Car Works in Tokyo; b. 1874 in Kyoto; edu. at Doshisha and the Tokyo Imp. Univ. in Mechanical Engineering; is Mng.-Dir. of the Japan Car Works, Ltd., in which the interest of the Amano family is predominant. Add. Honjo Aioi-cho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. of the Asano Cement Co. and several other undertakings started by his father Soichiro Asano; b. 1889, second son; edu. at Harvard in Economy, class '12. Add. Mita Tsunamachi, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: mechanical engineer and partner of the Kuhara and the Kaijima interests, being connected with both families by marriage; b. 1880 in Yamaguchi-ken; edu. at Eng. Coll. of Tokyo Imp. Univ., class '03; served for some years at the Shibaura Eng. Works and then went abroad for study and inspection. Add. Ushigome Sanaicho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Man.-Dir. of Russo-Japanese Fishery Co., Ltd.; b. 1875 in Nagasaki-ken; grad. in Law, Tokyo Imp. Univ., '99; was Mng. of Wakamatsu Branch of the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; then Mng. of Sapporo Branch of Hokkaido Colliery Steamship Co., Ltd.; present post in '23. Add. Myogadani, Koishikawa, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Mng.-Dir. of Tokyo Building Co.; b. 1866 in Echigo; studied law and became Judge in '93 and transferred to the Foreign Office same year; attached to Consulate at Fusan in '93; Consul at Jinsen, Shanghai, Shashi, Sydney and Hankow between '94 and '05; Consul-Gen. at Shanghai, '05-09; then at Chientao till '12; Con.-Gen. at Honolulu, '12-14. Add. Tozuka, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Pres. of Nippon Sugar Refinery Co., etc., Dir. of various concerns; b. 1865 in Karatsu; grad. at Keio-Gijuku, '90; was in the service of Mitsui Bussan; then entered the present Co. after the notorious scandal culminating in the suicide of its former President; Chairman of Tokyo Chamber of Commerce till '25 as successor of Visc. Shibusawa. Add. Shiba Shirokane, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Pres. and Mng.-Dir. of the Oji Paper Manufacturing Co. since '11; b. 1868 in Nagano-ken; grad. from Keio, '91 and then took to journalism in the provinces; entered the Mitsui Bank and was transferred to the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha and had charge of its Branches at Shanghai and Taihoku, '15. Add. Azabu Shin-ami, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: 2nd Baron, Mem. House of Peers; Dir. of Onoda Portland Cement Mfg. Co.; b. 1886 in Yamaguchi-ken; grad. from Eng. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., '01; Lecturer at Kyoto Imp. Univ., '02-04; Army technical expert, '04-06; despatched to Europe and America on official mission, '08-09; was also on the faculty of Waseda Univ. Add. Yotsuya, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Lieutenant (ret.), Dir. Gov. Sericultural Institute at Nakano; b. 1867 in Saitama-ken; grad. in Agriculture, Tokyo Imp. Univ., '92. Add. Nakano, near Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Prop. of Haneda Belt Mfg. Co.; b. 1871 in Kyoto; studied cotton thread belt with his brother and invented it which patented in '99, afterward completed manufacture of rubber belt and others. Add. Honjo Sotote-machi, Tokyo..

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. of Kisha-Seizo (Car Mfg.) Co.; b. 1872 in Osaka; grad. in Mechanics, Tokyo Imp. Univ., '96. Add. Tennoji, Osaka.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Crown Mem. House of Peers, Pres. of K. Hattori & Co., Ltd., that run Seikosha Watch and Clock Works, Dir. of First Mutual Life Ins. Co. and of Chosen Industrial Co., Ltd.; b. 1860 in Tokyo; established in business 1881 and incorporated '17. Add. Ginza Shichome, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: pioneer of rolling-stock makers in Japan, ex-Vice-Pres. Osaka Loco. Works; b. 1855 in Tokyo; went to U.S.A. in '71, and entered a rolling-stock shop, N.Y., returning home about '80; was overseer of the works at Shimoasai, till about '90, and started the Hiraoka Rolling-Stock Works at Honjo, Tokyo, which was fused with Osaka Loco. Add. Kojimachi Nagatacho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Mng.-Dir. of Taiwan Sugar Mfg. Co.; b. 1870 in Hiroshima-ken; grad. at Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. in '99; entered Mitsui Bussan Co.; afterward transferred to Taiwan Sugar Co. Add. Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Pres. of Hoshi Pharmaceutical Co.; b. 1874 in Fukushima; edu. at Tokyo Higher Com. School and later at Columbia Univ.; published monthly "Japan and America" in N. Y.; despatched to Europe to inspect industry; returning home in '07 started present Co.; was once elected M.P. Add. Shinagawa Gotenyama, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Prop. of Ikegai Iron Works; b. 1869 in Chiba-ken; began machine manufacture in '90, now manufacturing internal combustion engine and printing machine, etc. Add. Mita Shikoku-cho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Pres. of Kurobe Railway Co., Hida Cable Transport Co.; b. 1878 in Shiga-ken; grad. in Law, Tokyo Imp. Univ. in '04. Add. Kaminomiya-machi, Osaka.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: b. 1876 in Tamba; grad. from Politics, Waseda Univ.; further studied at Vienna Univ. and Berlin Univ.; a senior official of the Financial Dept., Korean Government, '04, and held various local posts; next secretaryship of the Korean Household Dept.; went to Europe and America on official mission, to inspect the colonial condition there, '00; resigned official post and went to South Sea Islands to start gum plantation. Add. Takata-machi, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. Keio Univ., Nippon Flour Co., Chiyoda Life Ins. Co., etc.; b. 1865 in Yamaguchi; grad. Keio Univ. and for several years was on the staff of the Jiji; served at the Nippon Ginko, '98-06; visited Europe and America, '05 on official business; left the bank soon after his return, and restarted the defunct daily Nippon, '06, which was discontinued after some years. Add. Hakusan Goten-machi, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. Onoda Cement Co., Shibaura Iron Works, etc.; b. 1863 in Ishikawa-ken; grad. from Mitsubishi Nautical School, '83; Private Secretary to R. W. Irwin, adviser of the Union Transportation Co.,; then on a similar service to Mr. Masuda, of Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; had charge of the Co.'s London Office, '86-90; Mng. of the Osaka and Kobe branches, '90-95; then of the branch office at New York, '96; Mng.-Dir. of the Co's head office, '06; left in '14 being involved in the Naval Scandal. Add. Azabu Miyamura-cho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: 2nd Count, Pres. of Japan Steel Works at Muroran; Pres. of Taisho Bank; Dir. of Horai Life Ins., Hakodate Dockyard, Copper Mfg. Cos.; b. 1865, son of the late Adm. Count Kabayama; studied economics in England. Add. Nagatacho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Pres. of Katakura Raw Silk Mfg. Co.; b. '63 in Nagano-ken; adopted by K. Katakura as son-in-law in '77, runs about 36 mills through the country, besides shared in the business of Katakura Life Ins. Co., Nagano Sav. Bank, 19th Bank, Takabata Railway Co., etc. Add. Hirano-mura, Nagano-ken.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Eng., Dir. Shibaura Engineering Works; b. 1868 in Wakayama-ken; grad. in Eng., Tokyo Imp. Univ., '95. Add. Kirigaya, Osaki, near Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Mng.-Dir. of Shibaura Iron Works; b. 1869 in Nagasaki-ken; edu. at a Technical Apprentice School; entered the Shibaura Works and was twice sent abroad to inspect technical industries; succeeded in improving or inventing mechanical devices and appliances and was awarded the Blue Ribbon Medal. Add. Osaki, near Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Typewriter Manufacturer; b. 1875 in Tokyo; went to U.S.A. in his early years, and engaged by Eliot Hatch Co. typewriter manufacturers in New York for years; invented machine of Japanese script, now runs manufacturing mill at Kamata which is known by its welfare provision for labourers. Add. Kamata-machi, near Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Pres. of Ensuiko Sugar Co. and Karenko Timber Co., Dir. of the Taiwan Warehouse Co., etc.; b. 1866 in Niigata-ken; studied at Keio Univ.; was in the services of the Hokuetsu Railway Co. and Oji Paper Mill Co.; afterwards made a tour through Europe and America; entered the service of the Ensuiko Sugar Co. in '07 as its Mng.-Dir. Add. Ushigome, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Pres. of Japan Brewery Co., Dir. of other cos., Crown Mem. House of Peers (nom. 1928); b. 1843 at Okayama; came to Tokyo in '70 to find work with almost empty purse; started a lodging house; became acquainted with Baron Takashi Masuda and was appointed clerk of an exp. and imp. firm at Yokohama; transferred to the Mitsui Bussan Co.; left it '88 to start the Yebisu Brewery at Meguro; twice elected M.P. but has since abandoned politics. Add. Shiba Sakuragawa-cho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Man.-Dir. of Taiwan Sugar Mfg. Co., Nippon Artificial Fertilizer, Manju Life Ins. Co., Imperial Theatre, etc.; b. 1875 in Tokyo, eldest son of Takashi Masuda; educated in England; is also a popular amateur playwright. Add. Nihombashi Hama-cho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: ex-Pres. of the Kawasaki Dockyard, the Kobe Gas Co., the Kyushu Electric Tramway Co., the Kawasaki Steamship Co., etc.; educated at the Peers' School and the Tokyo Imp. Univ.; further studied in Europe and America; after returning home became Lecturer of the Tokyo Imp. Univ., which post he soon resigned to enter the business world; elected M.P. for Kobe in '21; involved in the financial trouble of the Dockyard and resigned its presidency in '27. Add. Yamamoto-dori, Kobe.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: ex-Pres. of South Manchuria R'ly Co.; b. 1880 in Yamaguchi-ken; edu. at Law, State Univ., Oregon, U.S.A.; passed Diplomatic Service Exam. in '04; Secretary of Kwantung Leased Territory; next at Foreign Office, Legation and then of Embassy; next Consul-Gen.; Vice-Pres. of South Manchuria R'ly Co., '27-29. Add. Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Prop. of Mikimoto Pearl Store (dealer in and originator of culture pearls); b. 1857 at Miye-ken; early started cultivation of pearl oyster, establishing a station in Ago Bay, Toba, which has won many prizes and medals at home and foreign expositions. Add. Ginza, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Prop. of Minorikawa Mill, manufacturers of sericultural machines; b. in Akita-ken; stud. sericulture at Nishigahara Sericultural Inst. in his early years; has invented many patent machines numbering about 150. Add. Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Prop. of the Marumiya Firm, manufacturer, wholesale dealer and exporter of toilet articles, drugs, soaps, etc.; b. 1871 in Tokyo and succeeded to his father's business in 1971; once Mem. of Tokyo Chamber of Commerce. Add. Nihombashi Tachibanacho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. of the South Manchuria Railway Co.; b. 1878 in Fukushima-ken; grad. from the Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., '02, passed the Higher Civil Service Examination, '02; entered the Finance Dept. as Secretary, '07; Dir. of the Banking Bureau of the same dept. in '16. Add. Yamashiro-cho, Dairen City.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Mng.-Dir. of the Toa Flour Mill; b. 1869 in Saitama-ken; grad. from Law, Tokyo Imp. Univ., '90; entered Keifu R'ly Co.; became Manager of the present Co. on its establishment in '06. Add. Hongo Yushima-Shinhanacho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. of Yokosuka Iron Works, Taihei Cotton Spinning, etc.; b. 1874 in Tokyo; studied at Peers' School; a clerk of Silk Exporting Co. at Yokohama; studied economics at Pennsylvania University, '03; served at the N.Y.K.'s Seattle Branch; the Chief of Mogi Trading Dept. and Mng.-Dir. of Mogi Co. till its liquidation. Add. Osaki, near Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Crown Mem. House of Peers, ex-Pres. of Nippon Petroleum Co., Dir. of Central Pet. Co., etc.; b. 1859 in Niigata-ken; elected Mem. of Niigata Pref. Assembly at his 20th year; M.P. in '94; organized Nippon Pet. Co. in '88; despatched on official mission to inspect petroleum business to America and Europe in '97 and again to U.S.A. in '04. Add. Azabu Zaimokucho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: former Vice-Pres. of Tokyo Subway Co. (resigned '27); b. 1881; grad. at Law, Tokyo Imp. Univ., '05; Per. Secretary to the Minister of Com. the same year; Secy. of the Govt. R'ly. Board till '20; Dir. Traffic Bureau, R'ly Dept., '20-24; Vice-Minister of Railways in '24. Add. Ushigome Kita-machi, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Chief of Government Iron Foundry; b. 1879 in Kumamoto; grad. from Law, Tokyo Imp. Univ., '03; entered the Dept. of Agr. & Com. where he was Secy. of one Bureau after another; Dir. of Patent Bureau and then of Forestry Bureau; later Vice-Min. of Agr. & Com.; present post in '25. Add. Yawata, Fukuoka-ken.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Baron (2nd), Mem. House of Peers (since '04), Mng.-Dir. of Toyo Iron Foundry, etc.; b. 1872 in Yokohama; son of late Baron Nobuyuki Nakajima, the first Chairman of the House of Representatives and Minister to Rome; grad. from the Tokyo Higher Commercial School and entered the stock exchange, '97; private secretary to late Prince Katsura and Marquis Saionji, as Premiers, '02-05; travelled abroad, '05; is interested in all the undertakings of the Furukawa family. Add. Ushigome Yakuoji, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Mng.-Dir. of Japan Petroleum Co., Ltd.; b. 186[illegible] in Niigata-ken; grad. from Law, Waseda Univ., '91, and has since been connected with the Co. Add. Nishi Okubo, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Mem. of Osaka Chamber of Commerce, Pres. of Platon Stationery Co., Prop. of Taiyodo Co., toilet manufacturer, and its chemical institute; b. 1881 in Yamaguchi-ken. Add. Naniwa-ku Mizusaki-cho, Osaka.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Vice-Adm. (ret.), Pres. of the Karafuto Petroleum Co. Ltd. created in 1925 as semi-official organ for exploiting the oil field conceded by the Soviet Government in '24; b. 1871 in Yamagata-ken; grad. from the Naval Cadet School, '93; steadily promoted till he was appointed a senior staff officer of the General Staff as a Rear-Adm. in 1918; Vice-Adm., '24, and appointed Commander of the Maizuru Naval Port. Add. Aoyama Minami-machi, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: ex-M.P., Dir. of Karafuto Petroleum Oil Co. and Teikoku Oil Co., Aud. of Dye-Stuff Manufacturing Co.; b. 1851 in Ibaraki-ken; studied in America; sent by the Government to Mexico and Brazil to inquire into emigration affairs, '03; has actively espoused the cause of free education and anti-juvenile smoking and drinking. Add. Mita Shikoku-machi, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Crown Mem. House of Peers (nom. '27), Pres. Union Beer Brewing Co., Dir. of Tobu R'ly Co., eto.; b. 1860 in Yamanashi-ken; took active part in village and provincial affairs; was one of the business-men who visited U.S.A. in the fall of '09 at the special invitation of American Chambers of Commerce; M.P. for some time. Add. Aoyama Minami-cho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D. Eng. (Japan), Pres. Tokyo Subway Co.; b. 1859 at Ogaki; grad. from Civil Eng., Tokyo Imp. Univ., '81; Eng. of Tokyo Prefectural Office, '81-86; studied in Europe and America as R'ly Engineer, '96-98; promoted to Chief-Eng., '10; Vice-Pres. of Imp. Govt. R'lys, '12; Pres. of the South Manchuria R'ly, '19-20. Add. Akasaka Shinsaka-machi, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Mng.-Dir. of the Obayashi-gumi, Ltd., Contractors for Civil Engineering and Architecture; b. 1885 in Fukushima-ken; grad. in architecture at Tokyo Imp. Univ., class '11. Add. Mikage-machi, Hyogo-ken.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Pres. of Toho Gas Co. (Nagoya) & Dir. of Tokyo Gas Co., etc.; b. 1878 in Hyogo pref.; grad. from engineering college, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; is authority on gas industry. Add. Nagoya.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Pres. Fuji Paper Mill, etc.; b. 1861 in Tokyo; married daughter of Visc. Shibusawa. Made a tour of inspection in Europe and America several times. Add. Mukojima Kommecho, Tokyo.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Baron, ex-Dir. of the South Manchuria R'ly; 3rd son and heir of the late Gen. Okura; grad. from Civil Eng., Tokyo Imp. Univ., '04; Eng. in the R'ly Dept.; Vice-Chief of the Transportation Dept. the S.M.R. and then Dir. of the Co., '25-28; visited Europe and U.S.A., '29. Add. Dairen.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: D.L., Dir. of South Manchuria R'ly. Co.; b. 1880 in Fukushima-ken; edu. at Tokyo Imp. Univ., politics, class '08; passed Dip. and Con. Exam., '10; Eleve-Con. in China, '10; in Ottawa, '14; Con. at Fuchow, '15; Sec. at Head Office, '17; Jr. Commissioner at the 1st congress of League of Nations at Geneva; 2nd Emb. Sec. at Washington in '20; Sec. at Head Office, '22; Dir. of Commercial Bureau, '27; present post in July '27. Add. Dairen.

a: Appendix A: Who's Who in Japan
t: Dir. of Sankyo Kabushiki Kaisha; b. 1880 in Yokohama; studied at Yokohama Commercial School and Yokohama English and Japanese Language School; started drug business in '99; went to America to study drug business. Add. Azabu Iigura-kata-machi, Tokyo.
